response_text: Yielding lets a thread voluntarily give up the CPU before its time slice ends, while pre-emptive switching forces a context switch when the thread’s time slice runs out. The OS handles both yield calls and timer interrupts as signals to switch threads. This allows cooperative yielding and pre-emptive multitasking to work together seamlessly.\n
